data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Expert intuition is not literally a posterior; the 'generative model' may be unknown.","A checklist could be a perfect algorithm, not a lossy list, in some domains."],"overturn_conditions":["The checklist is an exact algorithm matching the generative model.","The expert's intuition is revealed to be a worse approximation than the checklist (e.g., expert is miscalibrated)."],"shared_structure":["A lossy compression averaged many times converges to the lossy compression, not to the source.","Bias is not reduced by averaging; only variance is."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_003"],"transfer_claims":["Treat the checklist as a lossy codec and the expert as a direct estimator: averaging the codec output cannot recover information the codec discarded.","The signature of lossy compliance is systematic error with high agreement on the codec-divergent subset."]},"claim":"Atypical counterexample: on tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes and a known generative model, a single expert whose intuition is well-calibrated to the generative model can be strictly better than any non-expert panel with a checklist, because the checklist is necessarily a lossy compression of the generative model, whereas the expert's intuition can approximate the posterior directly. The panel's advantage from averaging is a variance reduction that cannot recover the bias introduced by the lossy checklist, and the single evaluation distinguishing evidence is the panel's systematic error on items where the generative model assigns low probability to the checklist-predicted answer.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If no expert is well-calibrated to the generative model, the counterexample fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist encodes the full generative model (e.g., an algorithm), the panel is not lossy and the argument fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the task is not governed by a compact generative model, the Bayesian framing does not apply.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the task has a verifiable generative structure P(outcome | features), an expert with well-calibrated intuition approximates the Bayesian posterior. A checklist encodes a discrete proxy rule, which is a lossy compression of P. The panel averages multiple applications of the same proxy, reducing variance but preserving proxy bias. On items where the proxy and P diverge, the panel is systematically wrong with high agreement (false precision). The expert, approximating P directly, is better. The distinguishing evidence is the panel's systematic error on the proxy-divergent subset, coupled with high inter-rater agreement: high agreement + high error on a defined subset = compliance tracking a lossy proxy, not genuine reliability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
